properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 6:01AM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central New Mexico and the Tularosa
Basin, including Otero County. Far west Texas including El Paso and
Hudspeth Counties.

* WHEN...Saturday evening through early Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of thunderstorms are expected to move through
South-Central New Mexico and Far West Texas. Widespread rainfall
amounts of 1" are likely with localized areas receiving 2-3"
resulting in flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH EARLY SUNDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 NM out
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 24 at 7:53AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry Tortugas
out 60 nm...

At 753 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots. This thunderstorm was
located 27 nm south of Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving
southwest at 10 knots.

The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM OVER THE WATERS

properties.areaDesc: Lower Koyukuk Valley; Middle Yukon Valley; Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 24 at 3:37AM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph expected.

* WHERE...Lower Koyukuk Valley, Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys, and
Middle Yukon Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A brief period of wet snow will quickly
transition to rain Friday afternoon. Wind will increase Friday
morning with peak gusts occurring between 4 PM Friday and 4AM
Saturday.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM AKDT THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Northern Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 24 at 3:36AM AKDT until October 25 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 12
inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including Broad Pass.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop north of Talkeetna and
across Broad Pass by late this morning or early this afternoon. The
heaviest snow is expected to fall between late this evening and
Sunday morning before tapering off. The snow may mix with rain at
times near the south end of the pass, limiting snow accumulations.
After a break break in the snow, another round of snow is possible
overnight Sunday into early Monday morning.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.
